description: Use when designing or refactoring classes, modules, or interfaces in any OO language — and whenever the user mentions SOLID, single responsibility / SRP, open/closed / OCP, Liskov substitution / LSP, interface segregation / ISP, dependency inversion or dependency injection / DIP/DI. Triggers explicitly on those names, AND implicitly whenever code shows the smells they target: a god class doing three jobs, a `switch`/`if-isinstance` on a type tag that grows with every feature, a subclass that throws "not supported", a fat interface whose callers use 2 of 11 methods, or a high-level class that `new`s a concrete database / mailer / HTTP client inside itself. Teaches all five principles with bad→good examples in both TypeScript and Python, a cross-cutting anti-pattern catalog (including over-applying SOLID), and one notification-dispatcher system refactored to honor all five together. Skip for throwaway scripts and genuinely simple CRUD/glue where an interface per dependency is pure ceremony — misapplied SOLID is needless indirection.
